title: Zigbee smart plugs turning off on their own randomly - Not Tuya TS001F Issue
body: Since upgrading to Home Assistant Core 2023.9.3, all my Zigbee smart plugs randomly turn themselves off, usually within a few minutes of one another. The logbook only says they “turned off”; no automation or manual button press triggered it. I initially suspected migrating to a new machine, but the same problem occurs after upgrading the old machine. Restoring 2023.8.4 stops it. I am using Home Assistant OS, ZHA, and what I described as a Sonoff Dongle-P.

symptoms_visible: On Home Assistant Core 2023.9.3, all my Zigbee smart plugs randomly turn themselves off, usually within a few minutes of one another.
The logbook only says the plugs turned off and does not show an automation or manual button press.
The plugs remain on normally after I restore 2023.8.4.
N0.label: N0 correlated plug shutdowns reported

symptoms_visible: Only my Woolley-branded plugs, identified by ZHA as Sonoff SA-030-1 devices, turn themselves off.
N1.label: N1 affected devices identified

symptoms_visible: About twenty minutes after I upgraded to 2023.10.1 and turned the plugs on, they turned themselves off again.
N2.label: N2 shutdown captured on 2023.10.1

symptoms_visible: After restoring 2023.8.4 and leaving debug logging enabled for a few hours, the plugs stayed on.
N3.label: N3 working-version comparison captured

symptoms_visible: On 2023.9.1 the plugs turned themselves off twice while debug logging was running.
N4.label: N4 regression narrowed to 2023.9.1

symptoms_visible: After I upgraded to the 2023.11 development build, the plugs still turned themselves off as they always had.
N5_x.label: N5_x development-build aftermath

symptoms_visible: After installing 2023.10.4, the plugs remained on for eight hours without turning themselves off.
N_terminal.label: terminal fixed build verified

question_patterns: Please download and upload device diagnostics for one affected plug, rather than only the ZHA integration diagnostics.
What manufacturer and model does ZHA report for the plugs that turn off?
Are plugs from other manufacturers affected too?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I uploaded the device diagnostic. They are branded Woolley here, but ZHA identifies them as Sonoff SA-030-1. Only those plugs are affected.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Several unrelated plug models from different manufacturers turn off, and their device diagnostics identify different Zigbee chipsets.
The label says Woolley, while ZHA still identifies the device as Sonoff SA-030-1.

question_patterns: Can you upload the ZHA device diagnostic for an affected plug?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Hopefully this is the right file: zha-18c9e8603b58b3ffb5155c5df3d49529-Sonoff.SA-030-1-f12d3f0f6f6db027e1ba2d3e4f1e8314.json-2.txt.

question_patterns: Which exact Sonoff coordinator model and firmware are you using?
Is this a ZBDongle-E with its stock firmware?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, it is a Dongle-E with the firmware that came with it.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: It is the same Dongle-E but I bought it from a different retailer.

edges.comment: Issue comments c4-c12 and c13-c14, reporter's system only: maintainers requested per-device diagnostics and clarified that the opening post's Dongle-P description was inaccurate; the reporter identified the affected Woolley devices as Sonoff SA-030-1 and confirmed a stock-firmware Dongle-E.

question_patterns: Can you update to a current 2023.10.x release and report whether the plugs still turn off?
Does the same behavior occur on 2023.10.1?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I upgraded to 2023.10.1. About twenty minutes later the plugs turned off again.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The plugs remain on normally for several days on 2023.10.1.
They turn off after thirty minutes rather than twenty minutes on 2023.10.1.

question_patterns: Enable debug logging from the ZHA integration menu, reproduce the shutdown, disable logging, and upload the resulting log.
Can you capture a ZHA debug log covering the moment a plug turns off?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I enabled debug logging from the integration menu and uploaded home-assistant_2023-10-11T20-47-45.750Z.log. The event was at about 20:57.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The log stops before the shutdown and contains no traffic from the affected plug around the event.
The same event is captured a few minutes earlier in another ZHA debug log.

edges.comment: Issue comments c13-c22, reporter's system: updating and capturing logs were handler-initiated measurements. The reporter supplied only the installed version, observed timing, and raw log file. The maintainer's conclusion that an OTA interaction precedes a plug crash is reserved for the final solution's engineer inference.

question_patterns: Can you restore the known-working version, leave ZHA debug logging enabled for a few hours, and upload the comparison log?
Please capture the same debug logging on 2023.8.4 when the problem does not occur.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I restored 2023.8.4, ran it for a few hours without the issue happening, and uploaded home-assistant_2023-10-12T16-35-53.917Z.log.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The plugs also turn themselves off on 2023.8.4 while the comparison log is running.
I collected four hours rather than a few hours of working-version logs.

edges.comment: Issue comments c22-c28, reporter's system: the maintainer requested a working-version comparison. Restoring 2023.8.4 changed the installed system state; the answer records only the reporter's observation and uploaded log, not the maintainer's interpretation.

question_patterns: Can you test the intervening 2023.9 releases to narrow down the first affected release?
Please install 2023.9.1, reproduce the behavior with ZHA debug logging, and upload the log.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I installed 2023.9.1 and uploaded home-assistant_zha_2023-10-14T11-11-49.388Z-9.1.log. I think the plugs turned off twice in that log.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: 2023.9.1 behaves like 2023.8.4 and the first shutdown only appears in a later release.
The 2023.9.1 log contains one shutdown rather than two.

edges.comment: Issue comments c27-c32, reporter's system: the maintainer requested release narrowing and the reporter installed older releases. This focused graph retains the decisive 2023.9.1 measurement and omits the redundant 2023.9.2 stop while preserving the raw user report rather than asserting a code-level regressor.

solution.intent: Assume the latest 2023.11 development build already contains the effective fix and upgrade to it.
solution.concrete_example: Upgrade to the current 2023.11 development build because the change associated with the closed issue should already be included there.

edges.comment: Issue comments c39-c47, participant6's suggestion followed by the reporter's own test: both users initially thought the development build fixed the issue, but each then observed further shutdowns. The graph uses only the reporter's installation and firsthand failed observation as the causal chain.

solution.intent: Treat the shutdown as a firmware crash or reboot of the affected eWeLink/Sonoff plug during ZHA's no-OTA-image exchange, use a build containing the corrected ZHA OTA-response handling, and verify that the plugs remain powered on before declaring resolution.
solution.concrete_example: Use a Home Assistant build containing the corrected ZHA OTA handling and monitor the affected plugs for longer than their normal failure interval. In the thread, the reporter installed 2023.10.4 and the plugs stayed on for eight hours; the change was later removed from the next patch because of a separate coordinator bug and was planned to return in a subsequent beta.
solution.inference_hint: The user supplied device diagnostics, version-specific observations, and raw ZHA logs. The maintainer inferred from the 2023.10 log that the plug asks for an OTA update and then crashes or reboots after the no-image response. Connecting the shutdown to that exchange, rather than to an automation or ordinary off command, is engineer-side analysis.

edges.comment: Issue comments c22, c35-c36, and c51-c59. The maintainer tied the crash to the newer no-OTA-image response, while the reporter later verified the corrective change firsthand on 2023.10.4 for eight hours. Subsequent removal and planned reintroduction are release logistics, included only as factual context and not scored as the technical fix.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: affected Woolley/eWeLink devices identified as Sonoff SA-030-1 crash or reboot during ZHA's OTA no-image response exchange, and that reboot leaves the plugs off; this is not an automation or manual off command.
The diagnosis must be grounded in the affected-device diagnostics, shutdown-time ZHA debug log, and working-versus-broken version comparison rather than inferred from correlated shutdowns alone.
Must recommend a Home Assistant build containing corrected ZHA OTA-response handling and ask the user to monitor the plugs beyond their normal failure interval before declaring resolution.
Must not treat installation of an allegedly fixed development build as sufficient: the reporter tested a 2023.11 development build and the plugs still turned off.
Resolution requires firsthand verification by the reporter; the graph establishes that the plugs stayed on for eight hours after installing the tested build containing the change.

persona_hint.experience_level: Fairly new Home Assistant user who can restore backups, install specific Core versions, enable integration debug logging with guidance, and upload diagnostics and logs, but needs explicit instructions for locating device diagnostics and log files.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and persistent; reports concrete timings and version results, asks follow-up questions when instructions or release availability are unclear, and avoids claiming certainty until the plugs have remained on for a meaningful period.
